title: Gimel Hebrew Letter (ג): Sound & Words
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Gimel (ג): its [g] sound, with example words like גַג (roof) and אַגַב (incidentally), plus interactive practice.

editorialIssues.detail: Some letter-recognition distractors use letters not introduced in this lesson. Beginner scaffolding can be improved separately from the approved source synchronization.

The source MATCH_PAIRS exercise keys its answer pairs to 'Short [a]'/'Long [a:]' duration labels, which contradicts the course's vowel-length rule (Modern Hebrew pronounces Patah and Kamatz Gadol identically as [a]). contentOverrides can only patch an exercise's content/tip/correctAnswer, not its pairs data, so there is no override path to fix the labels in place; held out rather than republishing a length claim baked into the graded answer data.

blocks.0: Gimel Hebrew Letter (ג): Sound, Words & Practice

3.tip: When the Hebrew letter Gimel (גָ) is marked with Kamatz Gadol, it produces the [ga] sound, not [gu].

8.tip: Kamatz Gadol represents the [a] sound. When paired with Gimel (גָ), it produces [ga].

9.tip: The vowel used with the letter גָ is Kamatz Gadol, which produces the [a] sound.

theory.heading: Meet Gimel
theory.intro: The third letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Gimel makes a steady [g] sound, as in “good.”
objectives: Read Gimel in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">גַג</bdi> (roof).

examples.heading: Gimel in real words
examples.intro: See Gimel in two new Hebrew words, and review the Patah and Kamatz Gadol vowel marks from earlier letters.
